title: Where do I find the money for my first property?
excerpt: Many buyers find a good deal and are just short of the 10% down payment. Sean goes through the four Fs of funding, and why raising income beats blaming property prices.

qa.context: Young buyers often spot a promising deal and find themselves short of the 10% down payment, or unable to qualify for a loan because of card debts and instalment plans. Many complain that salaries no longer keep up with prices.
qa.question: Where can a first-time buyer find the money for a property, and what should come first?
qa.quote: you should ask yourself how can you afford this
qa.answer: First save six months of expenses. Then the money comes from the four Fs: family, friends, financial institutions and fools. Borrow from family or friends only if you repay on time, keep your credit clean for the bank, and steer clear of being anyone's 'fool'. Above all, work out the income you need and how to reach it.

reasons.title: Six months of savings comes first
reasons.body: If you spend RM3,000 a month, have RM18,000 in the bank before you look at property. Paying the minimum on cards all year and clearing them with the bonus leaves nothing to invest.

reasons.title: Partners split the bad times too
reasons.body: Buying with a friend halves the down payment, but both names are liable. When the unit is empty, each of you pays half the instalment every month.

reasons.title: Beware anyone who wants your name
reasons.body: 'Fools' are people who lend their name and credit to someone else's scheme for a promised share. If a deal were certain to make money, nobody would need to share it.

reasons.title: Work back from the price
reasons.body: Banks lend roughly where the instalment is a third of income. A RM500,000 property costs about RM2,500 a month, needing about RM7,500 of income; ask what would raise yours from where it is.

actions: Save six months of expenses before you start viewing.
Clear card debts and instalment plans so they don't block your loan.
If family or friends help, agree repayment terms in writing and keep to them.
Never lend your name or credit for someone else's purchase.
Calculate the income your target property needs, and plan side work or skills to reach it.
qa.caveat: Sean notes that loan rates were around 4.5% to 4.8% in 2019, far below the 12% of earlier decades, and that first-home schemes and developer packages may reduce the cash needed for a new launch.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for this June 2019 video. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased.
